title: The house
description: Say where things are in a home.

explanation.summary: Spanish says where something is with a preposition, and the choice is narrower than English. The workhorse is en for “in” and “on”, de for “of” and “from”, and bajo for “under”.

sections.heading: The four you need most
sections.body: En is in or on: en la cocina, en la mesa, en el jardín. De is of or from: el vaso de agua, la casa de mi madre. Con is with: con el café. Sobre is over or on top of: sobre la mesa.

examples.es: El libro está en la mesa.
examples.en: The book is on the table.

examples.es: La llave está bajo el sofá.
examples.en: The key is under the sofa.
It is a glass of water.

examples.es: El cuadro está sobre la silla.
examples.en: The picture is on the chair.

sections.heading: A and the
sections.body: Say el or la when you mean a particular one, and nothing when you are just mentioning a room or a thing: vivo en Madrid, but trabajo en la cocina. The article is a matter of whether the listener knows which kitchen.

sections.heading: Where it is, and where it goes
sections.body: Location uses estar: la llave está bajo el sofá. Motion uses ir: la llave está bajo el sofá, pero pongo la llave bajo el sofá. The difference is whether the thing moved.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: Most places take de: en la cocina, de la mesa, bajo la cama.
Feminine: la cocina. It can also mean the cooking itself.
